segments.text: "I sat in the front row of the Long Terrace and watched a second-year lift three-forty. He did it rather well. I clapped." Perrin looked at the jersey. "I'm to lift nothing until the strapping's off. That's the twentieth of next month, and then it's a pail, and then two pails. I'm to stand no floor before the new year. I asked whether I might call off from a chair, and the healer said that he supposed nobody could stop me."

"It's in a box and you're holding it like a baby. I've a wall at six." She looked at the two of them, and at the jersey, and breathed out through her nose. "Stand up. Arms forward. Not up. Kiva, the hem's yours; you've a right hand. I'll have the neck."

segments.text: It took three of them, and it was not quick. Kiva hauled, and Anwen steered, and Perrin said that he was being very brave, in a voice that came out of a great deal of grey wool. Then his head came through, red, with the hair on end.
He stood on the laundry step in it, under the lamp.
"Four. Five. Now." Her aunt opened her eyes. "It's a five. It's a slow, lame five, with most of the push at the front of it."
